outlook: Wheat jumped Tuesday morning, with Minneapolis December spring wheat up about 11 cents near $6.41 and Chicago wheat up 11 cents, bouncing from oversold levels after Ukraine destroyed part of the Kerch Strait bridge and blocked a key Black Sea shipping channel used for Russian grain. December corn was up about a penny near $4.50 after a flash sale of 130,000 tonnes to Colombia, while January soybeans were up about 7 cents and ICE canola gained nearly C$7. Monday's NOPA report showed a record October soybean crush of 234.2 million bushels, and USDA's Crop Progress put the U.S. corn harvest at 88% and soybeans at 96%. Traders are watching new U.S. chip curbs on China ahead of Wednesday's Trump–Xi meeting at APEC, plus a strong U.S. dollar near 19-month highs.
